title: The AI emperor has no DAUs  why most devs still don't use code AI: Quinn Slack
talk_summary: Quinn Slack argues that despite hype, only ~5% of professional developers actually use code AI, and most usage is just autocomplete. He draws product lessons from Sourcegraph's Cody: build what you use daily, distrust customer feature requests, prefer manual/explicit modes before magic, and aggressively de-hype.

takeaways.technique: Dogfood-or-kill: only ship what the builders use daily
takeaways.what_they_do: They treat daily internal use by the builders as a hard gate: if the team building a feature doesn't use it every day, customers won't either, and 'it's awesome' feedback is a warning sign.
They build the explicit version first (user manually @-mentions context, agent works inside the editor where the dev can fix it) and only add automatic context injection after the manual path works.
takeaways.evidence_quote: first you got to make something work in manual and explicit mode

takeaways.technique: Ignore stated feature requests, measure actual behavior
takeaways.what_they_do: Customers repeatedly demanded fine-tuned models for a year; the team concluded the request was downstream of conference hype and what users actually wanted was 'it works well', so they discounted stated preferences.
takeaways.evidence_quote: every customer for about a year said I want fine-tuned models

takeaways.what_they_do: They rank AI features by usage frequency and how quickly a human can verify correctness; autocomplete wins because it's every keystroke and verifiable in ~100ms, while chat/agentic edits are rarer and slow to vet.
takeaways.evidence_quote: in a few seconds or even milliseconds 100 milliseconds you can figure out is this correct

takeaways.what_they_do: They deliberately set expectations low in pitches because recipients always inflate them; they cite Sam Altman doing the same even with far more validated products.
takeaways.evidence_quote: always explicitly dehype and set expectations low
